summary: Cachectic man with ESRD s/p deceased-donor kidney transplant on tacrolimus, severe idiopathic pulmonary hypertension and Stage 3a (T2N2M0) squamous cell carcinoma of the left lower lobe, recently discharged to rehab, re-presents from transplant clinic with hypotension (86/54, fluid-responsive), continued odynophagia, cough, anorexia and a further 5-lb weight loss (BMI 15.8). Labs show new neutropenia (ANC 750–890), thrombocytopenia (93K), anemia (Hgb 7.4) one week after last chemotherapy, mildly elevated Cr improving with IVF, and iron studies consistent with anemia of inflammation. Exam showed oral thrush; all cultures, Legionella and pneumococcal antigens negative and CXR unchanged, so antibiotics were stopped. He completed fraction 34/34 of XRT inpatient and improved with rehydration, mealtime analgesia, magic mouthwash, nystatin, appetite/energy stimulants and 2 units pRBC.
most_likely: Radiation esophagitis with odynophagia causing failure to thrive and hypovolemic hypotension

differential.diagnosis: Radiation esophagitis due to thoracic radiotherapy
supporting_evidence: Persistent odynophagia and pain with swallowing on re-presentation
Esophagus within radiation field; completed fraction 34/34 inpatient
Treated with magic mouthwash, mealtime oxycodone elixir, Maalox
Prior stay coded K208 other esophagitis / radiation sickness
opposing_evidence: No endoscopy or imaging confirmation this stay
Thrush also present and could contribute to odynophagia
differential.reasoning: Chemoradiation-induced esophagitis is the documented mechanism driving odynophagia, poor PO intake and the resulting dehydration/hypotension that prompted admission, making it the most defensible principal disease.

differential.diagnosis: Adult failure to thrive with severe protein-calorie malnutrition and cachexia
supporting_evidence: BMI 15.8, weight 94.7 lbs, 5-lb further loss since prior discharge
Anorexia, malaise, poor PO intake; dronabinol and Ritalin for appetite/energy
Cachectic on exam; nutritional supplementation, prior PEG refusal
opposing_evidence: Symptom rather than single organ disease; secondary to chemoradiation toxicity
differential.reasoning: Documented as the overarching reason for admission and heavily treated; strong candidate for principal or first-listed secondary diagnosis in coding.

differential.diagnosis: Hypovolemic hypotension due to dehydration and poor oral intake
supporting_evidence: Referred from transplant clinic for hypotension; ED BP 86/54 → 110/70 after 1L IVF
Note states 'hypovolemic hypotension' as reason for direct admission
Blood pressures normalized with IVF and increased PO intake
opposing_evidence: Hypotension is the admission mechanism, not the underlying disease
Chronic low baseline BP with pulmonary hypertension and off beta blocker
differential.reasoning: Clearly present and treated, but represents the presenting physiologic derangement secondary to malnutrition/esophagitis rather than the root disease.

supporting_evidence: Admission WBC 1.1, ANC 750, platelets 93, Hgb 7.4 one week post chemotherapy
Received 2 units pRBC; counts recovered spontaneously by discharge (WBC 6.8)
Prior stay coded D61810 chemotherapy-induced pancytopenia
opposing_evidence: No febrile neutropenia or documented infection
Anemia multifactorial with CKD low-EPO state and inflammation
differential.reasoning: Objectively documented cytopenias temporally linked to recent carboplatin/paclitaxel; a codable major complication of this stay.

differential.diagnosis: Acute kidney injury on chronic kidney disease in renal transplant recipient (prerenal)
supporting_evidence: Admission Cr 1.4, BUN 37, improving to Cr 1.2 with IVF
Note: 'AKI due to pre-renal azotemia; ESRD s/p DCDRT', true baseline nearer 1.1
Concentrated urine osm 580 with high urine urea
opposing_evidence: Creatinine elevation modest and below historical baseline of 2.3–2.5
No oliguria or electrolyte crisis documented
differential.reasoning: Prerenal azotemia superimposed on transplant allograft nephropathy, volume responsive; supportive secondary diagnosis with tacrolimus titration.

differential.diagnosis: Stage 3a squamous cell carcinoma of left lower lobe of lung
supporting_evidence: Biopsy-proven keratinizing SCC, T2N2M0 by PET-CT
CXR: continued left basilar necrotic LLL mass with small pleural effusion
Received final XRT fraction 34/34 during this admission
opposing_evidence: Cancer itself stable; admission driven by treatment toxicity, not tumor progression
differential.reasoning: Underlying malignancy under active treatment during the stay; codable but the toxicity/nutritional failure dominates this encounter.

differential.diagnosis: Oropharyngeal candidiasis (oral thrush) in immunosuppressed host
supporting_evidence: Admission exam: hyperpigmented tongue patches with '+thrush'
Started nystatin swish and swallow QID with resolution
Immunosuppressed on tacrolimus, post-chemoradiation, neutropenic
opposing_evidence: No fungal culture or endoscopy; possible esophageal extension not confirmed
differential.reasoning: Clinically diagnosed and treated infection contributing to odynophagia and poor intake; a distinct billable secondary condition.

differential.diagnosis: Severe pulmonary arterial hypertension with chronic cor pulmonale
supporting_evidence: RHC mPAP 55, PVR 10.4, CI 2.86; on macitentan/sildenafil
CXR: prominent pulmonary arteries suggesting pulmonary arterial hypertension
Loud systolic murmur; high-output AVF shunt contribution
opposing_evidence: No dyspnea, edema or hypoxemia this admission; 95–96% on room air
differential.reasoning: Chronic comorbidity actively managed with sildenafil in-house and limiting BP tolerance, but not the acute driver of this admission.

differential.diagnosis: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with nicotine dependence
supporting_evidence: Chart diagnosis of COPD; treated with standing and PRN nebulizers
Long smoking history, nicotine patch provided
Coarse basal crackles, worsening cough treated with antitussives
opposing_evidence: No wheezing on exam; cough attributed to necrotic tumor and radiation
differential.reasoning: Stable comorbidity requiring inpatient bronchodilator therapy; supports secondary
